task_specification.objective: Deliver the first player-facing Fusepoint increment: a cleanly booting native Godot 4.7 placeholder room where ordinary keyboard and mouse input can move and look, mouse capture can be predictably released and reacquired, and restart always restores the same initial state.

diagnosis.root_cause: The candidate is only the generated project shell: project.godot launches main.tscn, but main.tscn contains a single Node with no visible room, player body, Camera3D, input handling, or deterministic restart path. It therefore cannot yet provide the required runnable first-person bootstrap.

stop_conditions: Stop when the frozen prototype_bootstrap_boot_shell check has current host-owned pass evidence.
Do not import or bind the authored environment, production weapons or hands, HUD, minimap, enemies, decorative collections, online content, or later-phase mission systems.
Do not add visual polish beyond the geometry, lighting, and minimal orientation cues needed to prove a visible bounded room and stable camera.
Stop and report a blocker if the project cannot boot without missing resources or fatal Godot errors after focused repair.

strategy.rationale: Build directly on the existing minimal entry scene using only candidate-owned Godot primitives and one focused player controller. This closes the required boot-shell gap without pulling production content or later-phase systems into the first increment.

code: Parse and load project.godot, main.tscn, and scripts/prototype_player.gd with the configured Godot 4.7 runtime; require zero parse errors and zero missing-resource references.
Confirm the main scene contains one active Camera3D under the placeholder player, collision-backed floor and boundaries, and input actions for forward, backward, left, right, and restart.
Confirm all resources are candidate-owned built-ins or local source files and that no production asset families or network dependencies were added.
runtime: Developer focused check: launch from a fresh process, verify the bootstrap reaches the room without a black frame or fatal error, then exercise WASD and mouse look through ordinary input.
Developer focused check: release capture with Escape, reacquire it by explicit click, and verify neither transition changes authoritative player position or introduces a camera jump.

Developer focused check: move and rotate away from spawn, trigger restart at least twice, and verify the same spawn transform, zero velocity, initial camera orientation, and captured-input state each time.
GameLoop Runtime and QA Tester recapture the candidate at 1280x720 and issue the formal prototype_bootstrap_boot_shell verdict; runtime evidence collection and gap closure remain host-owned.
visual: The shipped gameplay view clearly shows a simple bounded room, visible floor, walls, neutral lighting, and enough asymmetric orientation cues to make movement and turning observable.
Reject black screens, visible void, floor fall-through, clipped spawn framing, unstable horizon, missing surfaces, production-content leakage, or debug-only proof.

Treat the supplied Fusepoint effect-imagination image as later art-direction context only; this intentionally rough bootstrap must not imitate its final HUD, weapons, industrial map, enemies, objectives, or effects.

done_when: Launching the project opens a visible, non-black bounded placeholder room with a floor, enclosing walls, neutral light, and simple orientation cues; no external or production assets are required.
A Camera3D starts from a fixed safe transform inside the room and remains upright and stably framed with no visible void or immediate collision overlap.
Ordinary WASD input moves the placeholder player within the room and mouse motion changes yaw and pitch with a bounded vertical look range.
Mouse capture is deterministic: gameplay starts captured, Escape releases it, and an explicit click reacquires it without causing a camera jump.
The configured restart input reloads or resets the bootstrap to the exact initial player transform, camera orientation, velocity, and capture state on every attempt.
The room prevents ordinary movement from falling through the floor or escaping its bounds; this remains a bootstrap-scale proxy rather than production locomotion or world work.
The project uses native Godot scenes, nodes, physics, input actions, and scripts; it boots without missing-resource, parse, or fatal runtime errors.
No authored map, weapon or hand rig, HUD, minimap, enemy, objective system, decorative asset pack, or runtime download dependency is introduced.
tasks.instructions: Replace the empty generated scene with a minimal native first-person bootstrap. Configure explicit movement and restart input actions in project.godot. Construct a small bounded room from built-in meshes and collision shapes, add neutral lighting and a few restrained orientation cues, and place one fixed safe player spawn. Implement a focused CharacterBody3D controller with a child Camera3D for WASD movement, mouse look, pitch clamping, predictable mouse capture/release, collision-backed grounding, and deterministic restart. Keep the implementation deliberately rough and self-contained; do not begin later-phase locomotion features, objectives, product UI, asset intake, or final art direction.
tasks.title: Build the runnable first-person bootstrap shell
